items.sentence1: As soon as Clara arrived, it started to pour with rain.
items.after: it started to pour with rain.
fullAnswers: sooner had Clara got there than

explanation.en: Part 1: after 'No sooner' the auxiliary comes before the subject, 'had Clara'. Part 2: the past participle 'arrived' is followed by 'than', not 'when' or 'that'. 'Got there' instead of 'arrived' is also accepted.
explanation.cs: Část 1: po No sooner následuje inverze s past perfect: had Clara. Část 2: příčestí arrived a spojka than (ne when, ne that). Uznává se i got there místo arrived.

items.sentence1: I really regret not taking the job in Lisbon.

explanation.en: Part 1: 'If only' expresses regret, and a regret about the past needs the past perfect, 'I had'. Part 2: the past participle 'taken' (or 'accepted') completes it; there is no 'not', because the regret is about what did not happen.
explanation.cs: Část 1: If only + past perfect vyjadřuje lítost nad minulostí: only I had. Část 2: příčestí taken / accepted. Zápor nepatří, lituji toho, co se nestalo.

items.sentence1: A professional stylist is going to cut my hair tomorrow.
fullAnswers: will be having my hair cut

explanation.en: Part 1: the causative 'have something done' in the present continuous, 'am having my hair', expresses a future arrangement. Part 2: the object is followed by the past participle 'cut'.
explanation.cs: Část 1: have something done v průběhovém čase pro domluvenou budoucnost: am having my hair. Část 2: příčestí minulé cut (sloveso cut má tvar cut-cut-cut).

items.sentence1: It was difficult for us to find a parking space near the stadium.
items.after: a parking space near the stadium.

explanation.en: Part 1: the adjective 'difficult' becomes the phrase 'had difficulty'. Part 2: 'have difficulty' is followed by the -ing form, with optional 'in': 'finding', not 'to find'.
explanation.cs: Část 1: have difficulty = mít potíže. Část 2: po této vazbě následuje -ing tvar (případně in + -ing), nikdy ne to find.

items.sentence1: My doctor told me that I should eat less sugar.
fullAnswers: that I should cut down on
that I should cut back on

explanation.en: Part 1: 'advise' takes the pattern object + to-infinitive, 'advised me to'; 'advised that I should' is also correct. Part 2: 'eat less' becomes the phrasal verb 'cut down on' (or 'cut back on'), which needs 'on' before 'sugar'.
explanation.cs: Část 1: vazba advise somebody to do something: advised me to; správně je i advised that I should. Část 2: frázové sloveso cut down on / cut back on = omezit; bez on je odpověď neúplná.

items.sentence1: Although it rained heavily, the match went ahead.
fullAnswers: in spite of the heavy rain
in spite of it raining heavily
in spite of the heavy rainfall

explanation.en: Part 1: 'although' is followed by a clause, but 'in spite of' needs a noun phrase or -ing form. Part 2: 'it rained heavily' becomes 'the heavy rain' (or 'heavy rainfall', 'it raining heavily').
explanation.cs: Část 1: although + věta, ale in spite of + podstatné jméno nebo -ing. Část 2: větu převedeme na podstatné jméno: the heavy rain (také heavy rainfall, it raining heavily). Pozor: in spite of it rained je chyba.
